pitfalls.what: Engine.New defaults trustedProxies to all IPv4 and IPv6 CIDRs while forwarded client IP handling is enabled.
pitfalls.consequence: Unconfigured applications can accept spoofed X-Forwarded-For/X-Real-IP values, affecting IP-based controls and audit data.

pitfalls.what: WriteHeader ignores status changes after headers/body have already been written and emits only a warning.
pitfalls.consequence: Handlers cannot surface a late status override as an error; the original response status remains.

pitfalls.what: combineHandlers rejects chains reaching the abortIndex-derived limit with a panic.
pitfalls.consequence: Deeply nested middleware groups can panic during route registration instead of returning a typed error.

mandatory: add or update a regression test in *_test.go

damage_control_rules: Do not write credential-like paths (.env, secrets.*, *.pem, *.key).
Do not expose Authorization values in recovery logs.
Reject malformed trusted-proxy CIDRs via SetTrustedProxies.
Treat CodeQL, Trivy, and gosec findings as security gates.

logs: Trivy and CodeQL SARIF security reports

D1_topography.evidence_summary: go.mod identifies a Go module and README/Makefile identify Gin as a Go HTTP framework with Make-driven repository procedures; tracked metadata also includes Markdown, YAML, JSON, HTML-template, and shell-style configuration surfaces.

evidence.excerpt: Gin is a high-performance HTTP web framework written in Go.
If your pull request introduces a new feature, document it in [`docs/doc.md`](docs/doc.md), not in the README.

D2_module_boundaries.evidence_summary: The package graph separates root gin, request binding, response rendering, codecs, internal utilities, and ginS; package-level validator and JSON API variables are shared process state.

D3_type_contract.evidence_summary: binding.Binding is a real Go interface contract with two methods and an observed flow through concrete binders, Context APIs, factory selection, tests, and documentation.

D4_conventions.evidence_summary: Tracked Go files use lowercase package files, PascalCase exported APIs, camelCase internals, receiver methods, middleware factories returning HandlerFunc, returned errors, and prefixed logging streams.

D5_pitfalls.evidence_summary: Observed pitfalls include the wide default trusted-proxy CIDRs, silent late status writes, and the hard 63-handler registration limit.

evidence.excerpt: This is NOT safe if your app is behind a reverse proxy.

D6_validation.evidence_summary: Makefile and CI define repository validation: make test, fmt-check, vet, golangci-lint, tag-aware matrix testing, and high Codecov thresholds.

D7_operational.evidence_summary: Gin is a Go library rather than a repository-owned service: consumers run applications with go run, Engine.Run defaults to port 8080, and tags invoke GoReleaser with builds skipped.

D8_security.evidence_summary: Security-sensitive surfaces include trusted-proxy configuration, Basic Auth constant-time comparison, recovery-log Authorization redaction, zero-access credential path patterns, and CI CodeQL/Trivy/gosec controls.

D9_process.evidence_summary: The repository documents GitHub issue triage and PR review, requires tests and feature documentation, targets master, and uses CI on push/pull requests plus tag-triggered releases.

concerns.concern: HTTP route tree and request dispatch
concerns.one_line: Owns route registration into per-method radix trees and request-time matching, parameter extraction, handler selection, and redirect/error fallback.
concerns.covers: Engine registration and ServeHTTP dispatch, RouterGroup path composition, trie insertion/lookup, and route helper tests.
concerns.excludes: Middleware semantics, static-file internals, trusted-proxy extraction, renderer implementations, and listener lifecycle.

flows.name: Route registration
flows.description: Verbs compose paths and handlers before attaching them to a method trie.

steps.what_happens: RouterGroup verbs calculate absolute paths and combine handlers.
Engine.addRoute validates inputs and sizes pooled context buffers.
node.addRoute splits prefixes and inserts static, parameter, or catch-all nodes.
joinPaths and safeUint16 support path composition and sizing.

flows.name: Request dispatch and fallback
flows.description: The engine resolves a URL and runs the handler or miss fallback.

steps.what_happens: ServeHTTP resets a pooled Context and calls handleHTTPRequest.
node.getValue walks edges and returns handlers, Params, fullPath, and TSR hints.
handleHTTPRequest chooses redirect, 405, or 404 behavior.
Engine tests pin redirects, registration failures, re-entry, literal-colon updates, and route listing.

invariants.rule: The wildcard child remains final and node priority accounts for descendants and its own handler.
invariants.why: Lookup and priority reordering rely on this convention.

invariants.rule: Registration precedes serving and is not concurrency-safe.
invariants.why: Trie mutation and one-shot route updates are unprotected.

invariants.rule: Fallback order is trailing-slash, fixed-path, method-not-allowed, then not-found.
invariants.why: The order is externally visible.

invariants.rule: UseEscapedPath overrides UseRawPath and affects parameter unescaping.
invariants.why: The engine chooses path representation before lookup.

pitfalls.risk: Registering literal-colon routes after the one-shot route update.
pitfalls.consequence: New escaped paths can fail to match.

pitfalls.risk: Changing wildcard ordering or skipped-node rollback.
pitfalls.consequence: Greedy parameters can shadow static routes.

pitfalls.risk: Changing joinPaths or safeUint16 without updating pool assumptions.
pitfalls.consequence: Nested paths or parameter buffers become incorrect.

entry_questions: Is this registration or dispatch?
Does the path introduce wildcard, escaped-colon, raw-path, or extra-slash behavior?
Which fallback should win?

concerns.concern: HTTP response writer and Reader rendering contract
concerns.one_line: Owns staged response status and size, header commitment, interface delegation, and render.Reader header/body copying.
concerns.covers: ResponseWriter and Reader behavior through Context/Gin integration and tests.
concerns.excludes: Routing, handler composition, logging/recovery, template/JSON serialization internals, and listener setup.

flows.name: DataFromReader response
flows.description: A reader response stages status, writes headers, commits on body copy, and is finalized by the engine.

steps.what_happens: DataFromReader constructs render.Reader and calls Render.
Reader.Render writes Content-Type and missing headers, adds Content-Length, and calls io.Copy.
responseWriter.Write commits headers before forwarding bytes and increments size.
handleHTTPRequest performs final WriteHeaderNow for empty responses.

flows.name: Hijack and streaming lifecycle
flows.description: The wrapper preserves safe fallbacks and header-before-body behavior.

steps.what_happens: Hijack rejects body-written responses and delegates or returns ErrNotSupported.
Tests pin status, size, flush, and hijack transitions.
writeHeaders preserves existing header overrides.
Reader rendering succeeds without an optional Headers map.

touchpoints.role: Core writer state machine and interface.

Trusted semantic closure attached this tracked dependency: tracked path-local implementation/test mirror.

invariants.rule: WriteHeader stages status and WriteHeaderNow commits once; body writes and Flush commit first.
invariants.why: Renderers need a header window after status staging.

invariants.rule: Reader emits Content-Length only for non-negative lengths and only fills absent headers.
invariants.why: Unknown lengths remain unset and overrides survive.

invariants.rule: Hijack is allowed before body bytes and unsupported writers return ErrNotSupported.
invariants.why: This preserves websocket compatibility and normal fallback.

pitfalls.risk: Treating Status as an immediate commit.
pitfalls.consequence: Header ordering becomes incorrect.

pitfalls.risk: Reusing Reader.Headers across renders.
pitfalls.consequence: Content-Length mutation can race.

pitfalls.risk: Assuming every writer supports Hijacker or Flusher.
pitfalls.consequence: Streaming or fallback behavior changes.

entry_questions: Does the change occur before final WriteHeaderNow?
Is content length known?
Can the writer lack Hijacker or Flusher?

concerns.one_line: Owns debug-print gating, access-log formatting, panic recovery, broken-pipe handling, and Authorization redaction across built-in middleware.
concerns.covers: Debug hooks, Logger constructors/formatters/skips, Recovery handlers/request dumps, and exact tests.

flows.description: Recovery classifies panics and masks Authorization in diagnostics.

steps.what_happens: Recovery defers recover around c.Next and classifies broken-pipe sentinels.

flows.description: Route/template lifecycle events share the mode-gated diagnostic pipeline.

steps.what_happens: Route registration and template loading invoke debug helpers.

invariants.rule: Logger captures path before c.Next and status/errors/body state after it; Default installs Logger before Recovery.
invariants.why: The log must see the recovered final status.

invariants.rule: Recovery treats EPIPE, ECONNRESET, and http.ErrAbortHandler as broken pipes without writing status.
invariants.why: A dead client cannot receive a 500.

invariants.rule: secureRequestDump masks Authorization lines and debugPrint is silent outside debug mode.
invariants.why: Diagnostics avoid credential leakage and release noise.

pitfalls.risk: Reordering Logger and Recovery.

pitfalls.risk: Handling broken pipes as ordinary panics.

pitfalls.consequence: Variants continue to be logged.

concerns.one_line: Precomputes Basic credentials, compares authorization values in constant time, and stores the principal or aborts with the correct origin/proxy challenge.
concerns.covers: Account preprocessing, Base64 construction, matching, context keys, challenge headers, and 401/407 behavior.
concerns.excludes: Authorization policy, sessions/cookies/CSRF, Bearer/JWT, request-body binding, and client certificates.

flows.name: Origin match or 401
flows.description: Configured accounts become a credential table and requests receive a user key or are stopped.

steps.what_happens: BasicAuth normalizes realm and delegates to processAccounts.
processAccounts validates accounts and precomputes encoded credentials.
The handler reads Authorization and uses ConstantTimeCompare.
Success sets AuthUserKey; failure sets WWW-Authenticate and aborts with 401.
Tests cover encoding, exact rejection, success storage, realm quoting, and chain stopping.

flows.name: Proxy match or 407
flows.description: The proxy variant uses a distinct header, key, challenge, and status.

steps.what_happens: BasicAuthForProxy selects its realm and captures processed pairs.
Its handler compares Proxy-Authorization and stores AuthProxyUserKey.
Failure sets Proxy-Authenticate and aborts with 407.
Proxy success and 407 tests verify the separate contract.

touchpoints.role: Trusted semantic closure attached this tracked dependency: tracked path-local implementation/test mirror.

invariants.rule: Empty account sets or usernames panic during middleware construction.
invariants.why: Misconfiguration is surfaced before serving.

invariants.rule: Matching compares complete encoded values with ConstantTimeCompare.
invariants.why: Exact matching prevents false authorization.

invariants.rule: Failure aborts the chain and emits its challenge/status pair.
invariants.why: Unauthenticated handlers must not execute.

invariants.rule: Success exposes the principal through AuthUserKey or AuthProxyUserKey.
invariants.why: Those keys are the downstream contract.

pitfalls.risk: Mutating Accounts after installing middleware.
pitfalls.consequence: Captured pairs do not reflect runtime rotations.

pitfalls.risk: Treating an authenticated key as authorization.
pitfalls.consequence: Identity is accepted without route-specific permission checks.

pitfalls.risk: Changing realm quoting or using prefix matching.
pitfalls.consequence: Challenge or exact rejection behavior drifts.

entry_questions: Is this origin or proxy authentication?
Will accounts or realms change after middleware creation?
Does downstream code distinguish identity from authorization?

concerns.one_line: Owns content-type binding selection, decoder-specific request/body binding for non-JSON formats, lazy default validation, and the validation error contract.
concerns.covers: binding.Binding and BindingBody selection, MsgPack/TOML/XML/YAML decoders, defaultValidator traversal and initialization, and their implementation tests.

flows.name: Content type to decoded and validated object
flows.description: Context chooses a binding, the format implementation decodes into the destination, and the shared validator checks it.

steps.what_happens: Bind and ShouldBind choose binding.Default from request method and Content-Type, while format-specific shortcuts call MustBindWith.
Default maps XML, MsgPack, YAML, and TOML MIME values to their BindingBody implementations.

tomlBinding decodes with toml.NewDecoder and then calls validate.
xmlBinding decodes with encoding/xml.Decoder and then calls validate.
yamlBinding decodes with yaml.NewDecoder and then calls validate.
validate reaches the configured StructValidator, which lazily initializes validator.v10 and validates the destination.
TestMsgpackBindingBindBody verifies a decoded MsgPack field.
TestTOMLBindingBindBody verifies a decoded TOML field.
TestXMLBindingBindBody verifies a decoded XML field.
TestYAMLBindingBindBody verifies a decoded YAML field.

SliceValidationError.Error formats non-nil element errors with their original indexes.

concerns.concern: URL path canonicalization and allocation behavior
concerns.one_line: Owns canonical URL cleanup, repeated-separator normalization, trailing-slash semantics, and the allocation-sensitive helpers used before route lookup and proxy-prefix construction.
concerns.covers: cleanPath, removeRepeatedChar, their stack-buffer fast paths, route redirect lookup, forwarded-prefix sanitization, and path tests/benchmarks.
concerns.excludes: Radix-tree insertion and matching, route registration policy, and general request dispatch after the normalized path is produced.

flows.name: Request path normalization before lookup
flows.description: The engine normalizes a request path, then uses the canonical form for fixed-path redirect lookup.

steps.what_happens: Dispatch applies cleanPath when RemoveExtraSlash is enabled and uses cleanPath for fixed-path lookup.
cleanPath removes duplicate slashes and dot segments, prevents rooted .. traversal, preserves trailing slash intent, and returns the original substring when no allocation is needed.
TestPathClean and TestPathCleanLong pin canonical results and idempotence across ordinary and long paths.

flows.name: Forwarded prefix separator cleanup
flows.description: A forwarded prefix is sanitized before it is joined to the request URL.

steps.what_happens: handleHTTPRequest sanitizes X-Forwarded-Prefix and calls removeRepeatedChar before constructing the redirect path.
removeRepeatedChar detects repeated target bytes, lazily allocates only when needed, and preserves an already-normalized string.
TestRemoveRepeatedChar covers empty, unchanged, trailing, and repeated-slash cases.

flows.name: Allocation regression guard
flows.description: The path suite checks the no-change fast path and exposes short and long benchmarks.

steps.what_happens: TestPathCleanMallocs uses AllocsPerRun and BenchmarkPathClean/BenchmarkPathCleanLong report allocation behavior.
bufApp delays copying into a stack-sized buffer until the first actual change.

touchpoints.role: Core separator normalization and lazy buffer helper.
Trusted semantic closure attached this tracked dependency: tracked path-local implementation/test mirror.
Trusted semantic closure attached this tracked dependency: tracked path-local implementation/test mirror.

invariants.rule: Empty or relative paths become rooted and canonical; dot segments and repeated slashes are removed while a meaningful trailing slash is preserved.
invariants.why: Redirects and route matching expose these URL semantics.

invariants.rule: cleanPath is idempotent and its unchanged fast path avoids allocation.
invariants.why: Tests assert output stability and zero allocations on clean inputs.

invariants.rule: removeRepeatedChar changes only repeated target characters and preserves non-target content and trailing separators.
invariants.why: Forwarded-prefix redirects must not rewrite unrelated path data.

invariants.rule: The normalized path must be produced before fixed-path lookup or redirect construction.
invariants.why: Lookup against an unnormalized path changes externally visible route behavior.

pitfalls.risk: Changing .. backtracking or trailing-slash handling.
pitfalls.consequence: Redirect targets and route matching can change, including rooted traversal edge cases.

pitfalls.risk: Introducing an allocation on the unchanged fast path.
pitfalls.consequence: Hot request-path performance and allocation tests regress.

pitfalls.risk: Normalizing forwarded prefixes with a broader rewrite than repeated separator removal.
pitfalls.consequence: Redirect locations can be corrupted for unusual prefixes.

entry_questions: Does the change preserve rooted, dot-segment, and trailing-slash semantics?
Does cleanPath remain idempotent and allocation-free for already-clean input?
Is this request-path lookup or forwarded-prefix construction?
Can the helper be called with a long path that exceeds the stack buffer?

concerns.one_line: Owns the Render interface contract, content-type registration, concrete response serialization, and renderer error/header/body behavior across JSON and non-JSON response formats.
concerns.covers: render.Render and HTMLRender assertions, shared content-type handling, concrete JSON/XML renderers, and the broad renderer regression suite.
concerns.excludes: ResponseWriter status commitment and Reader streaming mechanics, which remain in the accepted HTTP response writer and Reader rendering contract concern; JSON backend selection remains in the accepted codec concern.

flows.name: Render contract to concrete response
flows.description: A renderer satisfies the shared interface, sets a content type when absent, serializes data, and writes or returns the underlying error.

steps.what_happens: Render declares Render and WriteContentType and compile-time assertions enumerate supported renderer implementations.
JSON-family implementations set content type, marshal through codec/json.API, and write bytes while propagating errors.
XML writes its content type and encodes the supplied value to the response writer.
Renderer tests verify content types, serialized bodies, and marshal/write failures for JSON-family responses.

flows.name: Header and write-error behavior
flows.description: Renderer implementations preserve caller headers and surface failures at the operation that writes the response.

steps.what_happens: writeContentType fills Content-Type only when the header is absent, preserving explicit overrides.
Tests use httptest writers and errorWriter to assert content type, body format, and errors from callback/data writes.
Additional tests exercise XML, protobuf, string/data, redirect, template, YAML, TOML, PDF, and Reader registrations through the shared contract.

touchpoints.role: Core response renderer contract and header policy.
Cross-renderer contract, serialization, header, and write-error tests.

invariants.rule: Every supported renderer implements both Render and WriteContentType; compile-time assertions protect the interface surface.
invariants.why: Context.Render relies on this shared contract.

invariants.rule: writeContentType does not overwrite an explicit Content-Type header.
invariants.why: Consumers can choose a more specific media type or charset.

invariants.rule: Serialization and writer errors are returned rather than swallowed.
invariants.why: The caller must be able to record failed response generation.

invariants.rule: JSON renderers use the selected codec/json API rather than a private encoder.
invariants.why: Build-tag-selected backend behavior must remain effective for responses.

pitfalls.risk: Adding a renderer without a compile-time assertion or contract test.
pitfalls.consequence: A response format can compile locally but fail integration or header semantics later.

pitfalls.risk: Overwriting caller-supplied Content-Type.
pitfalls.consequence: Negotiation and custom media-type behavior drift.

pitfalls.risk: Ignoring marshal or writer errors.
pitfalls.consequence: Handlers report success after incomplete or invalid responses.

pitfalls.risk: Changing JSON renderer calls without respecting codec/json.API.
pitfalls.consequence: Build-tag-selected backend behavior diverges.

entry_questions: Does the renderer implement both methods and have a contract assertion?
Should an existing Content-Type be preserved?
Are serialization and writer errors returned?
Does a JSON response still use the selected codec API?
Is the issue renderer behavior or response-writer commitment?

not_concerns.why_rejected: HTML template loading is an implementation behind render.Render and is covered by rendering concerns.
Static files wrap http.FileServer/StripPrefix with no distinct Gin-owned specialty.
Mode and debug printing are cross-cutting configuration glue, not a standalone specialty.
ErrorType/errorMsgs are a shared envelope consumed by binding, rendering, and middleware.
Benchmark instructions document checks but define no separate runtime contract.
Benchmarks measure adjacent behavior and are validation evidence rather than an independent specialty.
Contribution lifecycle guidance is a process artifact rather than application architecture.
